source_facts: Parcel 2.3 is a synthetic artifact uploader; this specification is authoritative. The command is parcel upload DIRECTORY, where DIRECTORY is the local artifact directory. The documented example directory is dist. --include-list PATH supplies a UTF-8 file containing one relative artifact path per line. Omitting --include-list selects every artifact in DIRECTORY. Supplying an empty include-list file selects no artifacts. --exclude-list PATH removes the listed relative paths from the selected set; exclusion wins when a path occurs in both lists. Selection lists are not shell glob patterns. The wire-size cap option is named --max-wire-kib. It limits the compressed payload of each artifact, not the aggregate upload. Its unit is KiB, with 1 KiB equal to 1024 bytes. An artifact whose compressed payload equals the cap is allowed; one whose compressed payload exceeds the cap is rejected. The batch-size option is named --batch-items and counts artifacts per request, not requests per second. --dry-run performs selection and size checks without uploading artifact payloads. --dry-run still contacts the server to verify the destination. --no-verify skips the post-upload read-back check and does not disable transport encryption. No default value for either numeric option is specified here. The example parcel upload dist --include-list release.txt --exclude-list private.txt --max-wire-kib 512 --batch-items 20 selects entries from release.txt, subtracts entries in private.txt, applies a 512 KiB compressed-payload cap to each remaining artifact, and groups at most 20 artifacts per request. At that cap, 524288 compressed bytes are allowed and 524289 compressed bytes are rejected. The examples assume that listed paths exist in dist. The reference covers selection and transfer options only; it makes no exit-status, authentication, retry, or aggregate transaction guarantee.

# Parcel 2.3 upload options

Use `parcel upload DIRECTORY` to upload artifacts from a local artifact directory. This reference describes the selection and transfer options used when preparing a release. In the examples, that directory is `dist`, and the paths written in the list files exist within it. The purpose of the selection section below is to explain how selection works. It provides an explanation of the selection behavior that applies when you choose artifacts.

## Select the artifacts

`--include-list PATH` reads a UTF-8 file with one relative artifact path per line. These entries are paths, not shell glob patterns. Supply the paths of the artifacts you intend to select rather than expecting wildcard expansion from the list reader.

The absence of a file and a file with no entries have different meanings:

- When `--include-list` is omitted, every artifact in the directory is selected.
- When `--include-list` names an empty file, no artifacts are selected.

`--exclude-list PATH` removes its listed relative paths from the selected set. If an artifact appears in both lists, exclusion wins. This is also how to read an invocation that includes an include list and an exclude list together: first identify the selected set, then subtract the exclusions. An empty include file therefore does not act as a request to select the whole directory.

## Bound the payload and request size

The compressed-payload cap option is `--max-wire-kib`. It applies to each artifact separately, rather than to the upload as a whole. The unit is KiB: 1 KiB equals 1024 bytes. Use the compressed payload size when comparing an artifact with this cap. The size of the complete upload is not the quantity being compared.

An artifact exactly equal to the cap is allowed. An artifact above the cap is rejected. For a cap of 512 KiB, a compressed payload of 524288 bytes is allowed, while a compressed payload of 524289 bytes is rejected. The equality case belongs on the allowed side of this boundary.

The batch-size option, `--batch-items`, counts artifacts per request. It does not express a rate in requests per second. For example, a value of 20 means at most 20 artifacts in a request; it is not an instruction to issue 20 requests each second.

## Preview and verification

`--dry-run` performs selection and size checks without uploading artifact payloads. It still contacts the server to verify the destination. Use this distinction when deciding whether a preview is suitable for the environment in which you are running the command. A preview avoids the payload upload but is not an offline operation.

`--no-verify` skips the post-upload read-back check. It does not disable transport encryption. The verification named by this option is the read-back operation, so its name should not be read as a general switch for every kind of verification or connection protection.

## Example

```sh
parcel upload dist --include-list release.txt --exclude-list private.txt --max-wire-kib 512 --batch-items 20
```

This invocation selects the paths in `release.txt`, subtracts those in `private.txt`, and applies the 512 KiB cap to each remaining artifact's compressed payload. It groups at most 20 artifacts into each request. The two numbers govern different quantities: one is an individual payload size, and the other is the number of artifacts in a request.
